In [[higher category theory]] in [[mathematics]], the '''pasting theorem''' guarantees that each pasting diagram has a uniquely defined composite that independent of the order of the vertical composite, as long as they are defined.<ref>{{harvnb|Johnson|Yau|2019}}</ref> Namely, such a cell is [[well-defined]] the several different sequences of compositions which the diagram could be explained as representing yield the same cell.{{R|Johnson1989}}

Operation of pasting appeared in {{harvtxt|Bénabou|1967}} when introducing weak 2-category.{{R|Johnson1989}} The pasting theorem for strict 2-category guarantees that every 2-categorical pasting scheme defines a unique composite 2-cell in every 2-category, this is proved by {{harvtxt|Power|1990}}.<ref name=HackneyOzornovaRiehlRovelli2023>{{harvnb|Hackney|Ozornova|Riehl|Rovelli|2023}}</ref> For weak 2-category it is proved in Appendix A of {{harvtxt|Verity|1992}}'s thesis as a consequence of the coherence theorem for weak 2-category.{{R|HackneyOzornovaRiehlRovelli2023}} The pasting theorem for strict ''n''-category was proved by {{harvtxt|Johnson|1989}} and {{harvtxt|Power|1991}}, but the definition of the pasting scheme used in that proof is different.

==Example for operation of pasting==
For the example, consider pasting diagram D for the triangle identity of an [[Adjoint functors#Definition via counit–unit|adjunction]]

[[File:Pasting theorem.svg]]

2-cell <math>\mathcal{E} : g \circ f \rightarrow \mathrm{id}_A</math>, <math>\eta : \mathrm{id}_B  \rightarrow f \circ g </math>

The entire pasting diagram represents the [[Vertical composition|vertical composite]] <math>(\mathrm{id}_f * \mathcal{E})(\eta * \mathrm{id}_f)</math> which is a 2-cell in D(A, B), this is the right-hand side of the diagram.<ref name=Johnson1989>{{harvnb|Johnson|1989}}</ref>

If a diagram in a 2-category were to be a 2-graph morphism from some 2-graph (that is 2-[[globular set]]) into the underlying 2-graph of the 2-category, then in the left-hand side of above pasting diagram, it would not be a "diagram" (in the sense of Johnson), that is, a cell drawn on a diagram it is may not defined as a composite of other cells.{{R|Johnson1989}}

Specifically, the codomain of <math>\eta * \mathrm{id}_f</math> and domain of <math>\mathrm{id}_f * \mathcal{E}</math> of the vertical composite <math>(\mathrm{id}_f * \mathcal{E})(\eta * \mathrm{id}_f)</math> do not equal:

<math> \mathrm{id}_B \circ f  \mathrel{\stackrel {\eta*\mathrm{id}_f} \longrightarrow} (f \circ g) \circ f \longrightarrow f \circ (g \circ f) \mathrel{\stackrel {\mathrm{id}_f * \mathcal{E}} \longrightarrow} f \circ \mathrm{id}_A</math>.

The pasting theorem guarantees that the vertical composite <math>(\mathrm{id}_f * \mathcal{E})(\eta * \mathrm{id}_f)</math> is uniquely defined.

==Pasting theorem for 2-category== 
===2-pasting scheme===
====Anchored graph====

Suppose <math>G</math> and <math>H</math> are anchored graphs such that:<ref>{{harvnb|Johnson|Yau|2021|loc=Definition 3.2.11.}}</ref>
* <math>s_G = s_H</math>,
* <math>t_G = t_H</math>, and
* <math>\mathrm{cod}_G = \mathrm{dom}_H</math>.

The vertical composite <math>HG</math> is the anchored graph defined by the following data:

(1) The connected plane graph of <math>HG</math> is the quotient

<math>\frac{G \sqcup H} {\{\mathrm{cod}_G = \mathrm{dom}_H\}}</math>

(2) The interior faces of <math>HG</math> are the interior faces of <math>G</math> and <math>H</math>, which are
already anchored.

(3) The exterior face of <math>HG</math> is the intersection of <math>\mathrm{ext}_G</math> and <math>\mathrm{ext}_H</math>, with

* source <math>s_G = s_H</math>,
* sink <math>t_G = t_H</math>,
* domain <math>\mathrm{dom}_G</math>, and
* codomain <math>\mathrm{cod}_H</math>.

:of the disjoint union of <math>G</math> and <math>H</math>, with the codomain of <math>G</math> identified with the domain of <math>H</math>.

====Definition of 2-pasting scheme====

A 2-pasting scheme is an anchored graph G together with a decomposition

<math>G = G_n \cdots G_1</math>

into vertical composites of <math>n \geq 1</math> atomic graphs <math>G_1, \dots ,G_n</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Johnson|Yau|2021|loc=Definition 3.2.13.}}</ref>

===2-pasting diagram===
Suppose <math>A</math> is a 2-category, and <math>G</math> is an anchored graph. A <math>G</math>-diagram in <math>A</math> is an assignment <math>\phi</math> as follows.

*<math>\phi</math> assigns to each vertex <math>v</math> in <math>G</math> an object <math>\phi_v</math> in <math>A</math>.
*<math>\phi</math> assigns to each edge <math>e</math> in <math>G</math> with tail <math>u</math> and head <math>v</math> a 1-cell <math>\phi_e \in A(\phi_u, \phi_v)</math>.

For a directed path <math>P = v_0 e_1 v_1 \dots e_m v_m</math> in <math>G</math> with <math>m \leq 1</math>, define the horizontal composite 1-cell <math>\phi_P = \phi_{e_m} \cdots \phi_{e_1} \in A(\phi_{v_0}, \phi_{v_m})</math>.

*<math>\phi</math> assigns to each interior face <math>F</math> of <math>G</math> a 2-cell <math>\phi_{F} : \phi_{\mathrm{dom}_F} \rightarrow \phi_{\mathrm{cod}_F}</math> in <math>A(\phi_{s_F}, \phi_{t_F})</math>.

If <math>G</math> admits a pasting scheme presentation, then a <math>G</math>-diagram is called a 2-pasting diagram in <math>A</math> of shape <math>G</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Johnson|Yau|2021|loc=Definition 3.3.1.}}</ref>

===Statement===
Pasting theorem for strict 2-category: every 2-pasting diagram in an strict 2-category has a unique composite.<ref>{{harvnb|Johnson|Yau|2021|loc=Theorem 3.3.7 (2-Categorical Pasting)}}</ref>

Pasting theorem for weak 2-category: every 2-pasting diagram in an weak 2-category has a unique composite.<ref>{{harvnb|Johnson|Yau|2021|loc=Theorem 3.6.6 (Bicategorical Pasting)}}</ref>

==Pasting theorem for Gray-category==

Every 2-dimensional pasting diagram in a [[Gray category|Gray-category]] has a unique composition up to a contractible [[groupoid]] of choices.<ref>{{harvnb|Vittorio|2023|loc=4.24. Theorem. }}</ref>

==Pasting theorem for strict ''n''-category (ver. Power (1991))==

Weak version of pasting theorem for strict ''n''-category:<ref>{{harvnb|Power|1991|loc=Theorem 6.10 (A weak n-categorical pasting theorem)}}</ref> for any positive natural number ''n'', every labelled ''n''-pasting scheme in an strict ''n''-category <math>A</math> has a unique "strong composite".<ref>{{harvnb|Power|1991|loc=Definition 6.8}}</ref>

Pasting theorem for strict ''n''-category:<ref>{{harvnb|Power|1991|loc=Theorem 6.16 (An  n-categorical pasting theorem)}}</ref> for every positive natural number ''n'', every labelled ''n''-pasting scheme in an strict ''n''-category <math>A</math> has a unique "''n''-pasting composite".
